sections.h2: How can I sell a house in Allen, Texas?
sections.html:
An Allen owner can list with an agent, sell without one, or accept a cash purchase offer, and the right choice depends on how much time and repair work the house can absorb. Allen sits in southwestern Collin County, on U.S. Highway 75, and the Census Bureau estimates 113,447 residents for July 1, 2025.

Most Allen homes are lived in by their owners, which means a well kept house meets a deep pool of owner-occupant buyers. A house with deferred repairs, a tenant in place, or a probate delay often fits a buyer who purchases as-is and closes on the seller's calendar.

  • Agent listing: the widest buyer exposure, with showings, buyer financing and inspection requests built into the timeline.
  • Sale by owner: you keep control of price and showings, and you handle the contract, disclosures and title steps yourself.
  • Cash offer: a single buyer, an as-is purchase and a closing date you choose, with the price reflecting the buyer's repair risk.

sections.h2: What do the Census numbers say about housing in Allen?
sections.html:
Allen is a high-income, high-value suburb with a large owner-occupied base. The Census Bureau's QuickFacts table for the city shows the figures below, and they frame what a typical buyer or renter in Allen looks like.

The city's population count was 84,246 in 2010, so Allen added roughly 20,000 residents in the decade that followed. The 2020 density was about 3,963 people per square mile, a compact suburban pattern.

sections.h2: How did Allen grow into the city it is today?
sections.html:
Allen began as a railroad stop. According to the Texas State Historical Association, an agent for the Houston and Texas Central Railway established the town in 1870, and it was named in 1872 for a former Texas attorney general who promoted the line. A post office opened in 1876, and by 1884 the settlement had a school, three churches, a chair factory and a flour mill.

Growth came late. The town had 1,940 residents in 1970 and 8,314 in 1980, a jump the Handbook of Texas ties to the economic growth of Dallas and Plano and the construction of Dallas-Fort Worth International Airport. By 2000 the population had reached 43,554.

That history explains the housing stock. Allen is a commuter city built mostly in the decades after 1970, so most sellers are dealing with homes that are decades old rather than a century old, and the questions that come up at sale are usually roofs, foundations and updates, not historic districts.

sections.h2: Which Allen city rules should a seller or landlord know about?
sections.html:
Allen has recently added a rental program that matters to anyone selling a house that was leased. At its October 13 meeting, the Allen City Council approved an ordinance creating a registration and inspection program for single-family rental properties, covering houses, townhomes and duplexes.

  • Annual registration fee: $150, with a $50 late registration fee.
  • Reinspection fee for ongoing compliance issues: $25.
  • The city planned to begin notifying owners in November 2026, and the initial registration deadline is January 31, 2027.
  • The city says single-family rentals make up about 14% of its housing but produced 38% of property violations, which is why exterior inspections are part of the program.

The city is matching ownership and utility billing records to find rentals. If you receive a notice for a house that is not a rental, the notice explains how to contact the city. If the home has been a short-term rental, ask Allen's permitting staff whether a rental permit is on file before you list.

For remodeling and repair permits, Allen's Building and Permitting Division is the first call. Open permits left behind by a prior owner can slow a closing, so ask for the permit history on the address.

sections.h2: How are property taxes handled when an Allen house is sold?
sections.html:
Collin County's tax assessor-collector bills and collects property tax for Allen, and the Collin Central Appraisal District values the property. Statements go out in October and are due on receipt, and the county's page says payment by January 31 avoids penalties. The Property Tax Office is at 2300 Bloomdale Road, Suite 2324, McKinney, and tax certificates and similar requests must be made at the McKinney office.

Homestead exemptions are filed with the appraisal district, not the county tax office. Collin CAD says the general exemption is filed between January 1 and April 30, early applications are not accepted, emailed applications are not accepted, and there is never a fee. A late application is possible up to two years after the taxes become delinquent.

Collin CAD's published table of rates and exemptions for 2023 showed these Allen city entries, and you should check the current year's table before relying on them:

  • General homestead: 5.00% of value with a $5,000 minimum.
  • Over 65: $50,000.
  • Disabled person: $25,000.

A seller who is 65 or older and keeps a school tax ceiling can move that ceiling to a new Texas home as a percentage, according to Collin CAD. Buyers, in turn, file their own homestead application for the year they close if the seller did not hold one.

sections.h2: How is the deed recorded in Collin County?
sections.html:
The Collin County Clerk records the deed. The clerk's land recordings page says a document must be an original or a clerk-certified copy, signed and notarized. The page also notes that some information is redacted from certain instruments in the online database under House Bill 4350, and that the online database is not the official repository of real property records.

Texas law requires a deed to be acknowledged before an officer such as a notary, or witnessed, before it can be recorded. Recording fees are set by the county, so ask the clerk's office for the current schedule rather than relying on an older fee sheet.

Closing is usually handled by a title company, which orders the tax certificate, pays off any liens and files the deed. A tax lien attaches on January 1 each year and follows the property, so unpaid prior-year taxes have to be cleared for a clean transfer.

sections.h2: What if the Allen house is inherited, in foreclosure or rented?
sections.html:
Each of these has a short Texas rule set, and a few dates drive most of the planning.

  • Inherited house: a will generally has to be probated within four years of death. A muniment of title can pass real property when no administration is needed, and the order and will are filed with the county clerk where the property sits.
  • Foreclosure: a borrower can reinstate within 20 days of the default notice. The sale notice must go out at least 21 days ahead, and sales are held on the first Tuesday of a month in the county where the house sits.
  • Tenants: a landlord generally gives at least three days' written notice to vacate unless the lease says otherwise, then files in justice court.

Selling before the foreclosure date, or before an eviction is finished, keeps more options open than waiting for the sale or the writ.

sections.h2: What should I check before accepting an offer on an Allen home?
sections.html:
Confirm the basics in writing before you sign. A short checklist keeps the closing on schedule.

  • Ask the Collin County Property Tax Office for the tax certificate and confirm no prior-year balance.
  • Check with Collin CAD that your homestead exemption and any school tax ceiling are on file and portable to your next home.
  • If the house was a rental, ask whether the city's rental registration applies to your address.
  • Ask the title company to search for open permits and unreleased liens.
  • Get the offer, the closing date and who pays each fee stated in the contract.

faqs.q: Does Allen require rental houses to be registered?
faqs.a: Yes. The Allen City Council approved a registration and inspection program for single-family rentals, including houses, townhomes and duplexes. Annual registration costs $150, with a $50 late fee, and the first deadline is January 31, 2027.

faqs.q: Who collects property tax on an Allen home?
faqs.a: The Collin County Tax Assessor-Collector collects it. The Property Tax Office is in McKinney, and Collin Central Appraisal District sets the value and handles exemptions.

faqs.q: When can I apply for a homestead exemption on an Allen house?
faqs.a: File between January 1 and April 30 with Collin CAD. The district does not accept early or emailed applications and charges no fee, and a late application is allowed up to two years after the taxes become delinquent.

faqs.q: Can I sell an Allen house if property taxes are unpaid?
faqs.a: Yes, but the taxes have to be paid at or before closing. A tax lien attaches on January 1 each year, so the buyer cannot take clear title until the balance is cleared.

faqs.q: How many people live in Allen, Texas?
faqs.a: The Census Bureau estimated 113,447 residents on July 1, 2025, up from 104,627 in the 2020 census.
